https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session on Tuesday, April 19, 2011 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, and this packet pairs the routine financial back-up — February and March 2011 treasurer's reports, check registers, ACH debit and wire transfer listings, and year-to-date budget reports — with the year's central fiscal decision. Agenda item 8.A asks the Board to authorize administration to implement approximately $6 million in budget adjustments and to draw on existing fund equity of approximately $7.6 million to address a 2011-2012 operating deficit the resolution estimates at between $13.6 million and $16 million. Supporting items include a 14 FTE certified staff reduction, a rescinded copy paper bid, a report on SMART Board training, and a resolution opposing diversion of the School Aid Fund to higher education.

## Meeting

Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Tuesday, April 19, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Packet page stamps run 4 through 207.

## Recognition and consent items

Sixteen teachers were nominated for the Troy School District Outstanding Teacher Award; three were forwarded to Oakland Schools — Caryn Leonard (fourth grade, Barnard Elementary), Ewa Ostrowski (ESL, Smith Middle School) and Trevor Smith (Physics, Troy High School). Leonard was also named the District's Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year lease of a car donated through the Suburban Collection. Sally Gibson, vice president of business development at Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union, recognized mini-grant recipients; Kerry Birmingham, director of community relations, opened the program. The consent agenda carries minutes of the March 1, 2011 meeting and the March 15, 2011 workshop, the February and March 2011 treasurer's reports, and a non-renewal teacher contract item that item 3.A proposes to delete.

## Personnel

Administrative resignations accepted with appreciation: Scott Bryan, Director of Technology (hired June 21, 2006), effective May 6, 2011; Judy Hunsberger, Principal, Morse Elementary School (hired June 22, 2005), effective June 30, 2011.

## Curriculum — T4 Study

Karl Schmidt of Consumer Insights, Inc. and Scott Bryan reported on the Troy Teachers Technology Training study, conducted with the Oakland University School of Business Administration. SMART Boards are installed in 367 classrooms out of 600, in three equal waves (January 2009, August 2009, August 2010); 170 of 293 qualified teachers completed the web survey. Teachers reported active use 29% of class time, passive use 43% and off or idle 28%, and reported improvement in student focus (91%) and engagement (89%).

## Business and other action

Item 8.A authorizes approximately $6 million in budget adjustments plus a draw of approximately $7.6 million of fund equity against a projected 2011-2012 deficit of between $13.6 million and $16 million, noting more than $57.9 million in budget adjustments since 2002. Item 8.B approves a reduction of 14 FTE in certified staff, with 10 teachers receiving layoff notice effective June 30, 2011. Item 8.C rescinds the March 1, 2011 award of Bid 9702 to D & P Management ($50,400.00); item 8.D awards copy paper to Contract Paper Group, Inc. (formerly RIS Paper) for $63,579.60. Item 10.A adopts a resolution opposing transfer of School Aid Fund dollars to community colleges and higher education; item 10.B schedules a Special Board Meeting for Tuesday, May 17, 2011.

**Recognition.** Sixteen individuals were nominated for the Troy School District Outstanding Teacher Award by peers, parents and students; a TEA selection committee chose three district nominees for Oakland Schools' county program: Caryn Leonard (fourth grade, Barnard Elementary), Ewa Ostrowski (ESL, Smith Middle School) and Trevor Smith (Physics, Troy High School). **March 1, 2011 minutes.** Called to order 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart; present Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Malven, Miletti and Mr. Hauff, absent Ms. Underwood; Superintendent Fowler and administrators Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Rajter, Stromayer, Witt and Birmingham attended with approximately 125 members of the audience. Mike Cianciolo, president of the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, and trustee Linda Braun announced $500 grant awards; the Foundation funded 85 grants and received the first installment of the Sharon Alexander Trust Fund in the amount of $400,000, dedicated to grants in drama and art. Resolution 11-026 added Item 6.A Administrative Resignation (Ayes 6, Nays 0). 11-027 approved consent items including the February 1 and February 15, 2011 minutes, the January 2011 Treasurer's Report, and bid awards for copy paper and Smart Interactive White Boards. 11-028 accepted the resignation of Frank Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, effective March 14, 2011. 11-029 adopted a limited Schools of Choice program for 2011/2012 under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, for grades 6-8 at Baker Middle School; Dr. Fowler projected 25 students registering. Under 11-030, Dr. Fowler noted the district made $6.2 million in reductions in 2010/2011 and $6.7 million in 2009/2010; Mr. Rajter presented proposed reductions totaling just over $4 million against an initial target of $6 million, rising to $8.4 million in cuts after the Governor's announcement. KinderPlus would become Kindersession, bringing parent tuition down from $3,000 to $2,500 for the school year. Ms. Philippart stated that out of 28 school districts five are operating in deficit and 14 districts have insufficient fund equities. Kris Karbon, Assessment Coordinator, reported all Troy schools made AYP for 2009/2010, that common core standards were finalized in June 2010 and adopted by 44 states, and that proficiency scores could drop by possibly up to 25%. Bria Ellis of Athens High School reported Charity Week February 7-11 raised $34,433.55 against a $21,000 goal. Resolution 11-031 went into closed session at 8:13 p.m. under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c); the meeting reconvened at 9:36 p.m. and adjourned at 9:37 p.m. Respectfully submitted, Paula Fleming, Secretary. The March 15, 2011 workshop was called to order at 6:10 p.m. with all seven members present and adjourned at 10:10 p.m., covering health care trends, Summer Success, community presentation feedback, budget update, superintendent evaluation process and board self-evaluation.

**Curriculum (item 7.A) — T4 Study.** A report, not an action, presented by Karl Schmidt, President of Consumer Insights, Inc. (5455 Corporate Drive, Suite 120, Troy, MI 48098, (248) 952-1600) and Director of Technology Scott Bryan, in partnership with the Oakland University School of Business Administration; Dr. Rich Machesky, Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction, was the initial district contact. SMART Boards are functioning in 367 classrooms out of 600, installed in equal waves in January 2009, August 2009 and August 2010; 170 of 293 qualified teachers completed the quantitative web survey after three qualitative sessions. Sample profile: K through 3 27%, fourth and fifth 25%, middle school 22%, high school 26%; General 30%, Sciences 17%, Math 14%, Language Arts 14%, Specials 13%, Social Studies 12%. Reported usage since the start of 2010-2011: active use 29%, passive use 43%, off or idle 28%. Impact on teaching, share reporting better: topical richness of lectures 80%, class time efficiency 73%, teachable moments 68%, speed of transitions 62%, teacher confidence 56%, face time with students 45%. Impact on students: focus 91%, engagement 89%, enthusiasm 84%, initial grasp 74%, long term retention 69%, sense of reward 44%. Willingness to complete training, assuming PD credit: 55% for 3 to 5-minute streaming snippets, 36% for 30 to 45-minute lectures, 27% for written "How To" manuals. Recommendations cover restructured initial training, a resource link list, fixing the TSD SMART Board Moodle site, and 1-hour "10 best" seminars during September professional development days; the deck notes the effort delivered a $35,000 research study for free.

**Business (item 8).** 8.A Authorization to Implement Budget Reduction Plan: the District has made more than $57.9 million in budget adjustments since 2002; reductions for 2011-2012 were presented March 1, 2011 and followed by four community forums; depending on the final approved School Aid Act, the District faces a 2011-2012 operating deficit estimated between $13.6 million and $16 million; the Board expects to pursue a three-year plan and authorizes approximately $6 million in budget adjustments plus a draw on existing fund equity of approximately $7.6 million. 8.B Reductions in Certified Staff, per a memorandum dated April 14, 2011 from Jasen M. Witt, J.D., Assistant Superintendent, Human Resources (4400 Livernois, 248/823-4000, fax 248/823-4014) to Superintendent Dr. Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D.: budget constraints led to a recommended reduction of 14 FTE in certified staff for 2011/2012, but because of a total of 20 retirements and resignations to date, a total of 10 teachers — those hired on or after August 16, 2010 — will receive layoff notification effective the end of the day on June 30, 2011, consistent with the Michigan Teachers' Tenure Act and the Troy Education Association contract, which requires notice no later than May 1st. One Baker Middle School teacher, Ms. Kara Spodarek, is recommended for non-renewal for unsatisfactory performance. 8.C Paper Bid Retraction: the March 1, 2011 award of Bid 9702 to D & P Management in the amount of $50,400.00 is rescinded after the vendor said it could not provide the specified product at that price; memorandum dated April 12, 2011 from Frank E. Lams, Purchasing Consultant, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077, to Mark S. Rajter. 8.D Awarding of Bid for Copy Paper: bids for 2,520 cases of 8 1/2 x 11, 20#, 92 brightness paper (500 sheets per ream, 10 reams per case) were opened February 17, 2011, sent to 17 potential bidders with 12 responding; Rock LLC and Sovereign Paper LLC tied at 25.000 per unit and $63,000.00 but could not honor their pricing, so the award goes to RIS Paper at 25.230, now known as Contract Paper Group, Inc., in the amount of $63,579.60 as an expenditure of the 2010-11 General Fund. Other tabulated bids: Midland Paper 25.245/$63,617.40; Global Office Solutions 25.790/$64,990.80; Global Associates Computers 26.490/$66,754.80; Paper Express 26.840/$67,636.80; Xerox 26.950/$67,914.00; AmeriSource 27.470/$69,224.40; A-1 Business Products 27.500/$69,300.00; Office Express 28.500/$71,820.00.

**Other (item 10) and Closed Session (item 11).** 10.A adopts a resolution opposing the diversion of School Aid Fund dollars to community colleges and institutions of higher education, reciting that school funding has increased by less than 1 percent per year during the past decade and that Michigan voters approved Proposal A in 1994, which shifted operating revenue to the State through an increase in the sales tax and did not include higher education in its ballot language. Adopted this 19th day of April, 2011, with a signature block for Nancy Philippart, President; Ida Edmunds, Vice President; Paula Fleming, Secretary; and Trustees Gary Hauff, Todd Miletti, Wendy Underwood and M'Liz Malven. 10.B schedules a Special Board of Education Meeting for Tuesday, May 17, 2011 at the Administrative Building following the Board Workshop, for personnel and business items and a closed session on the Superintendent's evaluation. 11.A resolves to go into closed session to discuss negotiations as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), with a roll call of Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti, Philippart and Underwood.
